text:
kevin: Heads-up — proposing a rolling kernel+driver+firmware validation next week to try and reduce GPU crashes / Xid frequency. Draft plan below, looking for quick 👍/concerns.

maya: high level — what’s the canary scope?

kevin: Start small: 2 nodes (one pt, one gt) in us-west1 as phase 0, 12–24h soak. If stable, expand by rack/day. Target changes: kernel 6.3.21 -> 6.3.27, nvidia-driver 535.86 -> 535.100, firmware bundle fw-2026-02. Everything deployed as a pinned upgrade artifact. Rollback image: redwood-node-2026-01 (pre-change).

oliver: What are the exact gating metrics / alerts we’ll use? Need BQ/Grafana queries to gate expansion.

kevin: Primary gates: Xid error rate per-GPU, ECC correctable/uncorrectable counts, CUDA driver resets, kernel oops count. Example queries (BigQuery):
```
-- per-gpu xid rate (1h)
SELECT gpu_id, COUNT_IF(message LIKE '%Xid%') / 1.0 AS xid_per_hour
FROM `redwood-telemetry.gpu_logs`
WHERE TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(ts, HOUR) = TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), HOUR)
GROUP BY gpu_id;
```
Also add a k8s-level smoke: `python infra/tests/gpu_smoke.py --short` after each node upgrade.

maya: +1 on those. Add kernel dmesg grep for Xid and a rolling count of "GPU ECC corrected". Also record nvml metrics: `nvmlDeviceGetTotalEccErrors`.

indra: For canaries we should enable verbose telemetry: set `REDWOOD_GPU_TELEMETRY=canary` and increase log level for redwood-agent on upgraded nodes so we capture nvml stacks and full dmesg, ship to kibana with tag `fw_canary=true`.

kevin: Drain/upgrade steps (short):
1) Label node: `kubectl label node <node> infra/fw-canary=true`
2) Drain: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
3) Upgrade image + driver + firmware via infra/ansible playbook `playbooks/fw_upgrade.yml --limit=<node>`
4) Run smoke tests: `infra/tests/gpu_smoke.py --short` and run 1h synthetic load (embedding generation 50 concurrent requests)
5) Observe gates for 24h; if exceeded -> immediate rollback (`ansible playbook rollback.yml --limit=<node>`) and `kubectl uncordon <node>`

kevin: If smoke fails, we abort expansion and roll back that node immediately. Documented escalation: if we see >2 nodes failing same day, escalate to eng-oncall and stop the rollout.

oncall-bot: Maintenance window approved: 2026-03-24 02:00-08:00 UTC. Pager: eng-oncall.

oliver: Cost/capacity note: draining nodes will reduce usable capacity. Expect ~7% capacity hit in region while canaries run. Schedule outside peak.

maya: I’ll create a Grafana dashboard with these panels and add an alert: `Xid rate per GPU > 0.5 / hour over 1h` or `ECC_uncorrectable > 0` -> page. Also will add a slack alert to #eng-oncall and a mute window for noisy transient spikes.

kevin: I’ll open the rollout PR with the playbook + checklist + rollback playbook. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/fw-validation/pulls/273. Tagging @oncall for visibility.

maya: Sounds good — I’ll own monitoring during the canary and handle immediate rollback if needed. :thumbsup:

indra: One more ask — capture pre/post kernel module symbols and nvml versions (script attached in PR) so we can diff vendors and drivermod timestamps.

kevin: Thanks — will include the symbol dump step in the playbook.

oliver: LGTM. Schedule and runbook look solid.

kevin: Great — plan to kick off phase 0 on Tue morning. Will post the node list in the PR and add a runbook link: https://docs.internal/redwood/fw-upgrade-runbook
